To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the kidney is the main organ for clearance of hemoglobin and that the epithelial endocytosis receptors megalin (LDL-receptor related protein 2) and cubilin (intrinsic factor-cobalmin receptor) are responsible for hemoglobin uptake in the proximal tubule.
megalin (and to a minor extent cubilin) are responsible for renal hemoglobin uptake.

megalin- and cubilin-mediated endocytosis of hemoglobin is a physiologic mechanism for renal clearance of hemoglobulin and that the uptake of hemoglobulin in the kidney is a prerequisite for its catabolic degradation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of megalin and the related receptor cubilin in renal clearance and degradation of hemoglobin.
the molecular mechanisms of renal tubular uptake and degradation of hemoglobin in the kidney.
the role of megalin and other endocytic receptors in renal clearance of proteins and peptides, including vitamin-binding proteins and hormones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
megalin, and to a lesser extent cubilin, are involved in hemoglobin uptake in normal kidneys and in the pathophysiology in conditions of hemoglobinuria.
megalin plays the main role in the uptake of hemoglogin in the kidney, whereas cubilin may assist under certain circumstances.
megalin, a member of the LDL receptor family, and cubilin, an integral membrane protein, are endocytic renal receptors for hemoglobin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
megalin/cubilin are the receptors for the renal clearance of hemoglobins.
megalin, the receptor for intrinsic factor-vitamin B(12) complexes, is also responsible for the uptake of hemoglobins in the kidney.
megalin/cubilin are responsible for renal uptake of hemoglobin and that the uptake occurs physiologically.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kidney is the main organ for clearance of hemoglobin in the body, and that megalin (and cubilin) is the main receptor for this process.
megalin, cubilin, and their ligand, hemoglobin, are involved in the pathogenesis of hemoglobinurias and tubulopathies.
the receptors megalin (LRP2) and cubilin (cubilin) mediate the uptake and clearance of hemoglobin in the kidney.
